transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-07
Time: 16:00 - 16:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Rohit (Redwood SE), Maya (BrightEdge PM), Carlos (BrightEdge Eng), Sophie (BrightEdge Sec)

Summary:
Short sync to confirm onboarding progress, unblock VPC access, review early latency numbers from the shadow runner, and align next sprint tasks (KV cache and tokenization tuning). Confirmed security asks and next steps for bench runs.

Topics: onboard progress; staging VPC & creds; latency bench results (shadow); KV/prefix cache tuning; security/KMS; schedule for narrower infra deep-dive.

[00:00] Avery: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick agenda: status, what's blocked, bench numbers rohit has, and then security follow-ups.
[00:22] Maya: thanks, yeah we, um, we only have about two engineers allocated this sprint so want to make sure we're prioritizing the right gating items.
[00:35] Carlos: hi, yes, we're focused on network and creds first. we spun up the staging V M but need the exact subnet ranges for the peering.
[00:48] Rohit: ok i have the shadow-run latency numbers from yesterday, i can share the sheet. quick note: the runner used a small 1k token prompt mix—it's synthetic but representative.
[01:05] Sophie: before we go deep, security point — we need clarifications on KMS integration, data at rest encryption, and audit logging retention. also SOC two artifact is required for our procurement.
[01:25] Avery: yes absolutely, i'll send the SOC 2 summary and the security pack; rohit can call out the K M S flow.
[01:35] Rohit: yeah so for KMS integration in private we support customer-managed K M S (we call it customer K M S) — the runtime will accept a wrapped key from their H S M /K M S and we decrypt within the secure enclave. (note: audio garble: "H S M" sometimes transcribed as "H S M" )
[01:59] Maya: and is that supported in the dedicated pool or only in private? our compliance team prefers private but capacity is a question.
[02:12] Rohit: private supports full KMS flow; dedicated can do envelope encryption but we need the agreement for key handling. i'll put the exact doc link in the notes.
[02:28] Carlos: on the VPC side, we need CIDR ranges and service endpoints. i dropped a doc in the slack channel but want to confirm the egress IPs from the runner.
[02:43] Avery: rohit, can you speak to egress IPs?
[02:47] Rohit: sure — hosted runners will NAT; for private there's static egress per region. i'll capture the egress list. one caveat: if you want per-AZ IPs, that's a separate config.
[03:05] Maya: good, that helps.
[03:09] Rohit: now quick walk through the bench. numbers are average p50 and p95 for text-gen path with 1k token window: p50~120ms per token, p95~520ms per token in our hosted shadow run but your staging with warm KV cache and continuous batching should be lower. important: these are noisy because synthetic traffic and token mix.
[03:36] Carlos: wait 120ms per token seems optimistic — are these on A100s or V100s?
[03:42] Rohit: sorry yes it's on A100 equivalent, 16b model quant. we did a quantized FP16 path. the sheet lists hardware — i'll share.
[03:52] Maya: can you also show cold-vs-warm cache numbers? our production will have a heavy prefix overlap so warm cache matters.
[04:03] Rohit: absolutely — cold p95 spikes to ~900ms per token; warm p95 drops to ~360ms. again sub-second but depends on KV cache hit rate. note: transcript sometimes shows "k V cache" as separate tokens.
[04:25] Sophie: from security side we also need to know retention of audit logs and token scrubbing — do you persist raw prompts?
[04:35] Avery: we have options — hosted keeps minimal logs by default, dedicated/private give you control. rohit, what's the default retention?
[04:43] Rohit: default is 30 days for request traces; you can request longer retention for premium. we also have an option to redact PII at ingestion. for private, customers manage retention via their logging stack.
[05:00] Carlos: ok good. about staging creds — we tried the key you provided but the role mapping failed, got a 403 from the gateway. error text was something like "permission denied: unauthorized-service".
[05:15] Rohit: that sounds like the service account doesn't have assume-role permission for the gateway role. double-check trust policy; i'll send the sample IAM policy.
[05:28] Maya: timeline check — our product timeline wants a small pilot by month end. is that still feasible?
[05:35] Avery: yes, as long as we get creds and we run the region bench early next week. main risk is staging networking.
[05:44] Carlos: our infra lead is OOO until Monday but i'll try to push the subnet details sooner.
[05:52] Rohit: fine, we'll prepare the bench with placeholder subnets and then run final once we have real ones.
[06:00] Maya: on tuning — you mentioned KV prefix caching and tokenization differences between our tokenizer and the reference. could that impact latency and quality?
[06:12] Rohit: yes, tokenizer mismatch can inflate token counts, increase cost, and change KV cache behavior. we recommend running our tokenizer shim in staging to measure delta. if the token count is +10-15% we'll need to retune batch sizes and cache window.
[06:32] Carlos: do you provide a tokenizer shim?
[06:35] Rohit: yes — small docker image we can push as artifact, or you can run the tokenizer script. i'll attach link.
[06:45] Sophie: re: compliance, do we get audit logs in the console or via syslog exports?
[06:50] Rohit: both — console UI shows token-level traces (redacted per settings); you can forward raw logs to your SIEM via syslog or cloud storage.
[07:02] Maya: any blockers on our side besides creds/subnet?
[07:06] Carlos: internal perf gating — our load simulation framework hasn't been wired to the runner but that's on us.
[07:13] Avery: ok action recap coming. oh and one customer ask — competitor comparison: they asked how we compare to Anthropic and Vertex. rohit quick elevator?
[07:24] Rohit: quick: Anthropic is model-focused with closed infra, Vertex ties to GCP infra; we emphasize unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, predictable latency, KV cache controls, and rollouts. cost/latency levers are more explicit here.
[07:40] Maya: that helps.
[07:44] Carlos: can we get a failover playbook — like if a region degrades, what auto-fallback is available?
[07:50] Rohit: yes, we support smart routing — you can configure region fallback to a compatible model variant. it can be automatic or can trigger a canary. i'll drop the runbook.
[08:03] Sophie: one last sec on KMS: any third-party HSM constraints? our security profile demands FIPS-validated HSMs.
[08:12] Rohit: supported, but for hosted we'd need to validate partner HSMs; private you run your own HSM. i'll flag this in the security doc.
[08:23] Maya: great. can we go through the sheet briefly?
[08:27] Rohit: sure — opening the latency sheet now (link shared in chat). p50 numbers stable; p95 varies by region. note the runner used smaller batch sizes to minimize tail latency. we can tune to match your target of p95 < 400ms for warm.
[08:50] Carlos: what batch sizes are you using?
[08:53] Rohit: for these runs batch size was 8 concurrent streams with continuous batching window 50ms, but with a production SDK you can optimize batching per route.
[09:06] Maya: ok we want a follow-up run that mirrors our real traffic distribution — i'll send a sample trace.
[09:13] Rohit: perfect, send trace and tokenization sample. we'll run the mirror in the shadow cluster.
[09:19] Avery: quick recap and owners — rohit will run per-region bench and share spreadsheet, carlos will push VPC/subnet and test SA, sophie clarifies KMS/HSM constraints, avery will upload SOC2 and pricing. schedule follow-up next week.
[09:40] Carlos: one more note — our infra will likely request static egress IPs per region; is that doable?
[09:46] Rohit: yes private has static egress IP per region; hosted is more dynamic but we can provide an egress block for enterprise. i'll document.
[09:55] Maya: any outstanding blockers from the SE side?
[09:58] Rohit: none beyond creds and traces.
[10:01] Avery: ok thanks all — we'll reconvene after the bench results.
[10:06] (meeting closes)

Reference links mentioned in call:

End transcript.
